name: Default browser and browser engine choice
plain: Becomes the app that opens web links.
meaning: The default browser sees every tapped link. Android has long allowed any browser; iOS added it in 14 and the EU and Japan added choice screens and engine freedom.

android.api_surface: RoleManager ROLE_BROWSER, intent filters for http and https
android.note: Any engine allowed; browser choice screens for EEA from 2024.

ios.permission: com.apple.developer.web-browser (managed entitlement); browser engine entitlements for EU and Japan
ios.prompt_ui: Settings > Default Browser App; EU choice screen at first launch of Safari
ios.store_policy: Apple approves browsers; alternative engines only in EU (iOS 17.4) and Japan (26.2)
ios.api_surface: Default browser entitlement; BrowserEngineKit; WebKit required elsewhere
ios.note: Other iOS browsers use WKWebView outside EU and Japan.

limits.headline: Can open your web links, after you pick it as your default browser
limits.user_action: You choose a browser in your default apps settings or on a choice screen
can: Open web links you tap in other apps
Use its own browser engine on Android
Show a choice screen in the EU on iPhone and Android
cannot: Become the default without your choice in Settings
Use its own engine on iPhone outside the EU and Japan
Open links if you switch back to another browser
limits.reach_label: Every web link, once you choose
limits.differs: Android allows any engine. iPhone browsers use Apple's WebKit outside the EU and Japan.

story.what_it_is: Chooses which app opens web links when you tap them.

marketing.name: Change default apps
marketing.pitch: Apple lets people choose a default browser and other apps in Settings.

story.for_you: You pick a default browser, and every link you tap in mail or chat opens there. In the EU and Japan you may see a choice screen on first use.
story.for_makers: Makers fight to be default, since the default browser sees every tapped link. Browser makers also get a say in search and ad choices.

use_cases.example: Tapping a link in a chat opens your chosen browser.
A default browser shapes which search engine and ad network people see first.
A game opens a web page for a login in your browser.
A shopping link opens in the browser that already has your cart.
A fake browser could steal links, so roles are checked.
A news link opens in an ad blocking browser.
A web app engine choice, like a different browser engine in the EU.

story.android_note: Any browser engine is allowed. A choice screen appears in the EEA since 2024.
story.ios_note: iOS added default browsers in 14. Outside the EU and Japan other browsers use Apple's engine.

history.change: EU choice screen and alternative engines
Japan browser choice screen and engines
